chapterName: Empire: The Severans and the Crisis of the Third Century (AD 193-284)

questions.question: What did Julia Domna do when her son Caracalla went on campaign?
options: She served as high priestess in Syria
She governed Rome alone as regent
She commanded a legion in the field
She travelled with him and handled official letters
She retired to her family estates
questions.explanation: Julia Domna accompanied Caracalla and handled much of the official correspondence herself, passing only major questions to him. She held the title of Augusta.
questions.sourceQuote: When her elder son Caracalla ruled and went on campaign, Julia Domna travelled with him and handled much of the official correspondence herself, passing only major questions to the emperor.

questions.question: Which territories did Zenobia's general seize in 270 while Rome fought the Goths? (select all that apply)
options: Egypt
Arabia
Dacia
Britain
Gaul
questions.explanation: Her general took Arabia and then Egypt in 270. By mid-271 her realm stretched from Ancyra to Upper Egypt.
questions.sourceQuote: In 270, while Rome fought the Goths, her general seized Arabia and then Egypt.

questions.question: Why did later third-century emperors keep mixing more bronze and copper into the coinage?
options: To fund new city walls
To replace silver lost to the Persians
To pay tribute to the Goths
To each pay a quick bonus to the troops
To build public baths in Rome
questions.explanation: Each new emperor needed a quick bonus (donativum) for his soldiers, so they debased the coins. Loyal soldiers were expensive.
questions.sourceQuote: Later emperors, each needing a quick bonus (*donativum*) for the troops, mixed in ever more bronze and copper.

questions.question: According to one account, how did the grandmother of the emperor known as Elagabalus persuade a legion to rebel?
options: By marrying him to the legion commander's daughter
By displaying an omen from the sun god
By promising each soldier a plot of land
By claiming he was Caracalla's illegitimate son
By forging a will of Septimius Severus
questions.explanation: One account says she claimed the boy was Caracalla's illegitimate son. He was actually a great-nephew of Julia Domna.
questions.sourceQuote: According to one account, his grandmother persuaded a legion to rebel by claiming he was Caracalla's illegitimate son.

questions.question: After the Severans briefly lost the throne in 217, how did Julia Domna's female relatives win it back?
options: They hired Parthian mercenaries to invade
They persuaded the Senate to depose the usurper
They married the usurper to a Severan princess
They poisoned the new emperor at a banquet
They used money and family claims to win over the troops
questions.explanation: Julia Domna's sister and nieces used wealth and family claims to sway the soldiers. They placed two of Julia Domna's great-nephews on the throne in turn.
questions.sourceQuote: After the dynasty briefly lost the throne in 217, these women used money and family claims to win over the troops and place two of Julia Domna's great-nephews on the throne in turn.

questions.question: What made the praetorian prefect who succeeded Caracalla a 'first' among Roman emperors?
options: First emperor elected by the Senate
First emperor not from a senatorial family
First emperor to rule from Antioch
First emperor to be a Christian
First emperor born in Syria
questions.explanation: Born into a Moorish family in North Africa, he was the first emperor without a senatorial background. He never set foot in Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: The conspirator, Macrinus, born into a Moorish family in North Africa, became the first emperor not from a senatorial family.

questions.question: The Plague of Cyprian, which raged from 249 to 262, was possibly which disease?
options: Measles
Typhus
Malaria
Smallpox
Bubonic plague
questions.explanation: The Plague of Cyprian was possibly smallpox. It may have cut the population of Alexandria by 62%.
questions.sourceQuote: The Plague of Cyprian, possibly smallpox, raged from 249 to 262 and may have cut Alexandria's population by 62%.

questions.question: Which actions of Caracalla's successor angered his soldiers? (select all that apply)
options: Paying new recruits less than veterans
Cancelling veterans' land grants
Refusing to march east against Persia
Disbanding the Praetorian Guard
Making peace with the Parthians by paying compensation
questions.explanation: The soldiers found his compensation payment to the Parthians humiliating, and his lower pay for new recruits angered them further. Troops in Syria soon backed a Severan rival.
questions.sourceQuote: He made peace with the Parthians by paying compensation, terms his soldiers found humiliating, and angered them further by paying new recruits less than veterans.

questions.question: Who were the coloni that emerged during the third-century crisis?
options: Slaves freed to serve in the legions
Tenant farmers bound to the soil for protection
Veterans settled in new frontier colonies
Tax collectors appointed by the emperor
Merchants licensed to trade with Persia
questions.explanation: Townspeople and small farmers traded their freedom for a landowner's protection, becoming coloni bound to the soil. This was an early model for medieval serfdom.
questions.sourceQuote: Many townspeople and small farmers traded their freedom for a landowner's protection, becoming tenant farmers bound to the soil (*coloni*), an early model for medieval serfdom.

questions.question: How did the first barracks emperor die in 238, the Year of the Six Emperors?
options: Killed fighting the Goths
Died of plague in Rome
Killed by his own troops amid Senate-backed revolts
Captured by the Sasanians
Executed on the Senate's orders
questions.explanation: He was killed by his own soldiers while revolts backed by the Senate raged. 238 saw six emperors in a single year.
questions.sourceQuote: In 238, the Year of the Six Emperors, he was killed by his own troops amid revolts backed by the Senate.
